**Brazil vs Norway (FIFA World Cup 2026, Round of 16, scheduled for July 5, 2026, at MetLife Stadium/New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey).**[[1]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/brazil-vs-norway-prediction-odds-picks-world-cup-match)[[2]](https://www.thestatszone.com/fwc26/matches/191922)

Only pre-July 3, 2026 information is used here (e.g., previews, squad updates, and historical data available before the match date). Post-match outcomes or later reports are ignored. ### Head-to-Head History (Especially Major Tournaments)
Norway holds a notable psychological and historical edge: they are the only national team Brazil has faced multiple times (four prior meetings) without a single victory for the Brazilians. The record stood at two wins and two draws for Norway.[[3]](https://totalfootballanalysis.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup-2026/world-cup-round-of-16-match-3-predictions)[[4]](https://brazilworldcupblog.net/2026/07/03/2026-world-cup-round-of-16-brazil-vs-norway/)

- The standout result was in the 1998 World Cup group stage (Marseille): Norway 2-1 Brazil (Tore André Flo and Kjetil Rekdal scoring late after Bebeto’s goal).[[5]](https://en.as.com/soccer/norway-vs-brazil-head-to-head-full-record-past-results-and-world-cup-history-f202607-n/)[[6]](https://www.facebook.com/CGTNSportsScene/posts/-brazil-are-stepping-up-their-preparations-for-sundays-worldcup-clash-against-no/1478594210968419/)
- Other encounters were friendlies, including 1-1 draws (1988 and 2006) and a Norway win.[[5]](https://en.as.com/soccer/norway-vs-brazil-head-to-head-full-record-past-results-and-world-cup-history-f202607-n/)

This unbeaten record against a five-time World Cup champion adds uncertainty despite Brazil’s overall pedigree and depth.[[3]](https://totalfootballanalysis.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup-2026/world-cup-round-of-16-match-3-predictions)

### Recent Form/Results
- **Brazil**: Under Carlo Ancelotti, they advanced from the group stage with a recent 2-1 win over Japan. ### Injuries or Suspensions to Key Players
- **Brazil**: Lucas Paquetá suffered a grade 2 left hamstring injury in the win over Japan and was considered unlikely to feature (intensive treatment ongoing, with slim recovery odds for the knockout stages). Raphinha was recovering from a hamstring issue (sustained earlier in the group stage); he had returned to training but was viewed as one game away from full availability and not expected to start. Casemiro was expected to be fit despite a prior concern.[[4]](https://brazilworldcupblog.net/2026/07/03/2026-world-cup-round-of-16-brazil-vs-norway/)[[10]](https://www.si.com/soccer/brazil-vs-norway-world-cup-preview-predictions-lineups-7-5-26)
- **Norway**: Erling Haaland was notably fatigued after scoring a late winner against Ivory Coast (“dead tired” and “on his last legs” in the second half per coach comments), raising questions about his freshness for a high-stakes match. Martin Ødegaard and others had been managed with rest in the group stage.[[8]](https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/recovery-question-worries-norway-fans-before-brazil-clash-2026-07-02/)

No major suspensions were widely reported in pre-match coverage. ### Travel Distance/Fatigue and Venue Conditions
Both teams were based in the US and had already played group-stage matches at MetLife Stadium, giving them familiarity with the venue, pitch (natural grass, converted for the tournament), and surroundings.[[11]](https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/mls/worldcup/2026/07/05/brazil-norway-preview-world-cup-metlife-stadium/90759053007/)

- **Conditions**: Expected afternoon kickoff temperatures around 83–85°F (28–29°C) with mid-to-high humidity and a chance of scattered thunderstorms (30%+ rain probability, increasing later). A flood watch was in effect for the region, with potential for performance-impairing heat (above ~28°C threshold linked to reduced running metrics). Lightning protocols could cause delays.[[12]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/brazil-vs-norway-world-cup-round-of-16-weather-update-forecast)[[13]](https://www.dailyrecord.com/story/news/new-jersey/2026/07/05/world-cup-live-updates-in-nj-as-brazil-faces-norway/90787848007/)
- **Fatigue factors**: Haaland’s tiredness was the main noted concern for Norway. Brazil’s deeper squad offered some mitigation for rotation needs. No extreme long-haul travel was highlighted for either side at this stage of the tournament. ### Crowd/Home Advantage and Other Storylines
MetLife Stadium (large capacity) was expected to see a significant Brazilian fan presence due to the large diaspora in the New York/New Jersey area, potentially creating an energetic, pro-Brazil atmosphere despite the neutral venue. Norway supporters were also anticipated in notable numbers.[[14]](https://www.northjersey.com/videos/news/new-jersey/2026/07/05/norway-and-brazil-fans-surge-to-metlife-stadium-for-world-cup-match/90814355007/)

Key narratives included:
- The matchup of Erling Haaland (Norway’s focal point) against Brazil’s defense versus Brazil’s attacking talents (e.g., Vinícius Júnior) and experience in knockout football. - Norway’s historical record adding motivation and tactical intrigue (physicality and counters vs. Brazil’s technical style). - Brazil’s need to adapt to absences (Paquetá, limited Raphinha) while relying on depth and pedigree for a quarterfinal push.[[3]](https://totalfootballanalysis.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup-2026/world-cup-round-of-16-match-3-predictions)[[10]](https://www.si.com/soccer/brazil-vs-norway-world-cup-preview-predictions-lineups-7-5-26)

These factors—particularly the H2H psychology, Haaland’s condition, injuries in Brazil’s midfield/attack, and venue weather—could influence tactics, such as Norway targeting set pieces or counters and Brazil emphasizing control and depth. Previews generally viewed Brazil as favorites on paper but noted genuine uncertainty due to the above elements.[[3]](https://totalfootballanalysis.com/competitions/fifa-world-cup-2026/world-cup-round-of-16-match-3-predictions)

Sources for facts are cited inline from web results (primarily previews and reports dated around or before early July 2026).

factors.impact: Significantly favors Norway. Brazil has a unique and notable historical record against Norway, having never defeated them in four previous encounters (2 draws, 2 losses), including a World Cup group stage loss in 1998. This establishes a strong psychological and tactical precedent.

Favors Norway. Lucas Paquetá suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury and is unlikely to feature. Raphinha is recovering from a hamstring issue and is not expected to start, weakening Brazil's creative midfield and attacking depth.

Favors Brazil. Norway's pivotal player, Erling Haaland, is reported to be 'dead tired' and 'on his last legs' after scoring a late winner in the Round of 32, raising concerns about his freshness and full impact for this high-stakes match.
Favors Brazil. MetLife Stadium is expected to see a significant Brazilian fan presence due to the large diaspora, providing an energetic, pro-Brazil atmosphere.

Favors Brazil. Brazil's deeper squad offers more options to mitigate injuries and provides extensive experience in high-pressure knockout matches, a clear advantage over Norway's less experienced squad in this stage.

Neutral to slightly negative for both. Expected temperatures of 83–85°F (28–29°C) with mid-to-high humidity and potential thunderstorms could lead to performance-impairing heat and a slower pace, potentially affecting both teams' energy levels and exacerbating Haaland's fatigue.

analysis.reasoning: While Brazil enters as the more established favorite due to their overall pedigree, squad depth, and anticipated crowd support, the model's prediction should be adjusted downwards for Brazil's win probability. The most compelling factor is Norway's unique historical dominance over Brazil, having never lost to them in four meetings, including a World Cup encounter. This head-to-head record introduces a significant psychological and tactical hurdle for Brazil. Furthermore, key injuries to Lucas Paquetá and a limited Raphinha weaken Brazil's attacking fluidity and creative options. These factors favoring Norway are partially counteracted by the reported fatigue of Norway's star player, Erling Haaland, which could diminish their primary offensive threat. The cumulative effect suggests a tighter contest than Brazil's reputation might initially imply, warranting a moderate negative adjustment to Brazil's chances.
